Tests, each shown red first: `test_a_link_whose_events_have_no_text_is_refused_and_writes_nothing`, `test_events_without_text_are_counted_not_written`, `linkEventsApi.test.ts` (red: a real Enron address read as events), and the keyboard case in `link-menu.spec.ts` that *Show emails* sends the brushed window and draws the Documents (red with the call unwired).

Build note (4 October 2026). All three steps of ADR-092 are built: step 1 `0c0e3d4`, step 2 `0e0b597` (with Amendment 1), step 3 in the commit that adds this note: `reader/DocumentReader.tsx` and `reader/readerApi.ts`, an overlay over the work area in `App.tsx`, and in `GlassCanvas.tsx` a double-click or Enter on a Document calls `onOpenDocument` rather than expanding. Tests shown red first: `DocumentReader.test.tsx` (before the component existed) and `keyboard/reader.spec.ts` (the canvas case red with the Document rule turned off); registry `READER_ACTIONS`. **Not seen:** the reader on the live Enron case.

### ADR-084, Amendment 3 (4 October 2026) — the case picker lists each case once, with its branches beneath it

Context. The owner, looking at *Choose a case*, asked why three "Enron corpus (real data, this machine only) · n selected" rows sat in the list beside the case they came from. They were branches made while testing *Branch selected*: each is a case of its own (decision 1), named after its parent. ADR-084 designed the tab strip and the Branches menu but said nothing about the picker, which listed every case flat and ignored `branched_from`. Owner's choice, from three: nested under the parent.

Decision. The picker lists each original case once, in its usual order, followed by every branch in its family, indented, oldest first, each labelled "branch" beside the caller's level. A family is grouped by the rule the tab strip already uses (`branchFamily`: a branch of a branch belongs to the original; if the original is not visible to the caller, the oldest listed ancestor heads the family, decision 4). No case is left out, and every row still opens and removes as before.

Tests, shown red first: `nestCases` in `cases.test.ts` (order, a branch of a branch, an unseen original, nothing dropped) and the picker case in `CasePicker.test.tsx` (red: the branch was listed apart from its case).

### ADR-092, Amendment 2 (4 October 2026) — correction: no email could be written as a Document; the ontology now declares what it carries

Seen by the owner on the live Enron case: *Show emails* put nothing on the canvas and *Extract entities* answered "'Document' does not declare properties 'event_id, message_id, sent_at' in its `properties` or `identifiers`". Both write an email as a `Document` with those three properties (ADR-089 step 3, ADR-092 step 1), and the ArcadeDB adapter checks every write against the ontology (`ontology/validation.py`), where `Document` declared only `title`; so every such write was refused, and no email ever became a Document on a real store.

Cause. Every test of those writes used a graph stand-in that kept whatever it was given: the third stand-in this week that accepted what the real dependency refuses (`CLAUDE.md` rule 15, after ADR-089 Amendment 1's lookup and ADR-084 Amendment 2's case filter).

Decision. `Document` declares `sent_at` (datetime), `message_id` (string) and `event_id` (string), all optional; the ontology version stays 11 for the reason ADR-079 gives (nothing a recipe writes, an index or an adapter reads changes for an existing load). An email without a message id is written without the property, never with a null the `string` type refuses. The stand-in now calls the adapter's own `validate_properties` on every node and link, so the two cannot disagree again. Tests: with the corrected stand-in, nine extraction and Show-emails cases failed with the owner's message before the ontology change and pass after; `test_an_email_without_a_message_id_is_written_without_one`. The API must restart to apply the schema (`make refresh`).

## ADR-093 — A selected node is seen: drawn larger with a bold ring, listed in the Inspector, and counted on the canvas

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as two multiple-choice questions after the owner said "the nodes do not get highlighted when I select them" and asked for the selection to be easier to navigate).

Context. Spec 02 §4 gave a selected node a "2px brass stroke, 1px surface gap". The code drew the 2 pixels and no gap, and the `@sigma/node-border` ring is drawn inside the node's disc, on nodes a few pixels across, so in the browser a selected node looked like any other: a screenshot of the keyboard harness with `n0` selected shows no brass at all. Nothing said "selected" anywhere else on screen except the strip's *Branch selected (n)*.

Decision.

1. **A selected node is drawn 1.6 times its size, with a brass ring (24% of its radius) and a surface-coloured gap (8%) inside it**, two border layers of its own (`selectionRing*`, `selectionGap*`), so the picture in the middle stays about its ordinary size; it is always named. Hover and a found path keep the interaction ring. Fill colour is never changed by selection (hue is entity type only).
2. **The Inspector lists the selection** when more than one node is selected: each by name; choosing one centres the canvas on it; each has a remove (×) that takes it out of the selection.
3. **A chip in the canvas corner says "n selected" with *Clear***, shown while anything is selected.

Consequences. Step 1 (this commit): `nodeAttributes.ts`, the two layers and the scale in `GlassCanvas.tsx`, `workingset/store.ts`'s attribute types; spec 02 §4's table. Found while proving it: the effect that redraws nodes whose selection or hover changed chose them by `borderSize`, so once selection had rings of its own a deselected node kept its rings; it now also redraws a node marked `selected`. Tests that would fail, shown red first: `nodeAttributes.test.ts` (the rings and their absence), and `keyboard/selection-look.spec.ts`, which counts brass pixels painted round a node (red at 0 with the ring shrunk to the old faint width, and red at 42 after deselecting before the redraw fix). Steps 2 and 3 follow with keyboard cases (rule 13).

Build note (4 October 2026). ADR-093 steps 2 and 3 are built: `inspector/SelectionList.tsx` in the Inspector's panel, fed by App's list of selected ids; `canvas/SelectionChip.tsx` in the canvas corner; the canvas handle's `centreOn` (pan and focus, selection kept) and `deselect`. Tests shown red first: the two components' unit tests (before they existed) and `keyboard/selection.spec.ts` (the chip case red with Clear unwired). Found on the way: the chip is a status region, so a keyboard case that found its message by `getByRole("status")` alone matched the chip; it now finds the message by its words. That case also showed the empty-expansion message still named a link type by its id in capitals ("linked by ASSOCIATE_OF"), a place ADR-091 should have reached; it now reads "linked by ‘Associate of’", the type's display name in quotes.

### ADR-092, Amendment 3 (5 October 2026) — Read full screen from the Inspector's opened email

Owner's request after the reader was built: the email opened in the Inspector "opens in a messy manner" in the narrow column, so it gains *Read full screen*. The reader reads a Document, and an email opened in the Inspector may not have been written as one yet, so the Inspector hands the reader the email itself (`readerViewOf`: the id it would be written under, `email:<event id>`, its subject, text, date, ends and link); the reader asks for the Document first and shows the handed email if there is none. Extracting from it writes the Document, and the reader reads that from then on. Found while building it: the server's reader named the link's source as the sender whatever the email's direction, where the Inspector's From reads an inbound email as sent by the far end; the reader now follows the direction. Tests shown red first: `LinkEvents.test.tsx` (the hand-over, and no button where nothing can show it), `DocumentReader.test.tsx` (the handed email shown when there is no Document), `test_an_inbound_email_is_from_the_far_end_as_the_inspector_says`, and the keyboard case in `link-events.spec.ts` (red with the button switched off).

## ADR-094 — Content the model can read: any record or entity may carry text, an image or a video, designated in the Ingest Studio, read and extracted from as Enron's emails are

Status: accepted 5 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as six multiple-choice questions over two rounds and answered in chat). It generalises ADR-089 and ADR-092 from Enron's emails to any content, from demo and real datasets alike.

Context. The owner asked for "the email idea" to extend to messages from phones and, in their answer, from "any device that has text, image or video content", and for the Ingest Studio to "allow objects to be designated as documents, images and videos that can be used by the LLM for entity extraction": "when modelling an object data type, the Ingest Studio must have the ability to designate whether the object has content that can be used for entity extraction". What exists: `ModelPort` already has `extract` (text), `transcribe` (audio, Whisper) and `describe_image` (vision, Moondream); the extraction pipeline and review queue exist; the deployment runs an object store (MinIO); spec 09 §7 describes an unstructured path (documents, images, audio and video, each with an extraction profile) that is not built; a structured recipe cannot say a column is content; the demo phone dataset (`demo_fixtures/cdr.py`) holds calls, not messages; ADR-089's email path reads text from an event's `excerpt` and is reached only on an email link.

Decision.

1. **Content comes in two shapes.** *On a link*: a message between two ends (an email, an SMS, a chat message) is an event on their link, as an Enron email is. *Held by an entity*: a photo, video or saved file on a device (or held by an endpoint, person or organisation) belongs to that entity.
2. **The Ingest Studio designates content, in both its screens.** In a structured recipe, when a source's rows are modelled, a column may be marked as content: *message text*, *document text*, or a *file reference* to an image or a video. On an event row the content belongs to the event (shape one); on an entity row it is held by the entity (shape two). The unstructured path of spec 09 §7 (files uploaded or pointed at: documents, images, videos) is built too, each file becoming content held by the entity the analyst names or standing alone. Designation is a declaration in the recipe, validated at save and at run like the rest of it; no expression language (rule 8).
3. **Every content item is a `Document` with a `media_kind`**: `text`, `image` or `video`. One type, so *Show messages*, the canvas, the reader and extraction work for all three; the ontology adds `media_kind` (enum) to `Document`. Files are kept in the deployment's object store, never in the graph; a Document carries a reference to its object.
4. **Held content is linked by a new relationship type, `HOLDS`**: from `Device`, `Endpoint`, `Person` or `Organisation` to `Document`, basis Direct (the source records the holding). This changes the ontology to **version 12**, and every published recipe is flagged once to be re-pinned (spec 09 §4's proactive flagging), as ADR-055 Amendment 1's bump did.
5. **Extraction by kind.** Text: `extract` as today. Image: `describe_image` gives a description and the text it reads (OCR); entities are extracted from that text, and the region of the image is the locator. Video: its audio is `transcribe`d and entities are extracted from the transcript, with the time in the recording as the locator; frames are not analysed. Face matching and biometric identification stay out of scope (spec 09 §7). Every finding is inferred until a person accepts it (rule 5).
6. **Reading.** The full-screen reader (ADR-092) shows text as today, an image with its description and the text read from it, and a video with its player and transcript. *Show emails* becomes *Show messages (n)* (named emails on an email link, messages on any other link whose events carry content), and a node holding content offers *Show content (n)*.
7. **The demo gains synthetic device messages and media** (rule 9: synthetic, in-repo): SMS with text on the phone dataset's links, and a few synthetic images and short videos held by its devices, so every path can be seen without a real dataset. Real datasets reach the same paths through the Studio, only on the owner's machine and under the real-data exceptions (rule 9, ADR-035 §C3).

Build order (owner's choice, each step usable on its own). **Step 1, messages:** the Studio's content marking on event rows, a recipe's message text written to the event and readable, the synthetic SMS, and the email path generalised (*Show messages*, Documents on the canvas, reader, extraction) to any link whose events carry text. **Step 2, media:** the object store, image description and video transcription, the reader's image and video views, the content marking on entity rows, and `HOLDS` (ontology version 12). **Step 3, files:** the unstructured screen of spec 09 §7 (upload or point at files) and synthetic held media in the demo.

Not decided here. Which archive formats are unpacked, and how deep (spec 09 lists one level); thumbnails on the canvas for an image Document; how long a video may be before transcription is refused or queued; whether a Document's file may be downloaded from the reader, and under what handling.

Consequences. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, to be written first in each step: a recipe that marks a column as content writes it so the reader shows it; a recipe that marks a non-text column as message text is refused at save; content on a link a principal cannot see is not readable (one refusal for hidden and missing); an image Document's description and OCR text are what extraction reads; a video's transcript is; a finding is inferred until accepted; a file is never stored in the graph; `HOLDS` refuses an end type it does not declare; the ontology at version 12 flags every recipe pinned to 11.

Built as ADR-081 decision 3 and Amendment 1 item 7 stated, with no new decision: `services/ingest/recipe_rules.py` refuses a recipe link naming a Probabilistic type, `SAME_AS`, `NOT_SAME_AS` or a type the ontology lacks; Map's save calls it (`422 recipe_rule`, each problem named, and the Glass shows those words rather than a status) and `run_recipe` calls it again after its ontology-version check, before any write. No recipe in the repository names a refused type (the one `SAME_AS` mention is a comment in `seizure_recipe.yaml`). An overlay type promoted as Direct (ADR-090 Amendment 1 item 2) is accepted once ADR-090's overlay is built, since the rule reads the ontology in force. ### ADR-094, Amendment 1 (5 October 2026) — ontology version 12, and a Studio run stores its events

Two things recorded as step 2 began. **Version 12** is in force (decisions 3 and 4): `Document` gains `media_kind` (text, image, video) and `object_ref`; `HOLDS` runs from `Device`, `Endpoint`, `Person` or `Organisation` to `Document`, Direct. Build note (5 October 2026). ADR-094 step 3 (files) is built: `DocumentContentService.upload` and `POST /v1/investigations/{id}/documents` (Editor; a marking the uploader could read and a legal basis required; a holder `HOLDS` allows and can see; the cap checked first; the upload's name check now takes the content kinds, since the studio's source list lacked `.mov`, `.webm`, `.webp` and `.gif`); the Glass's `AddFiles`, reached from the studio's new **Files** stage, from *Add files* under the canvas strip and from a holder's menu; the synthetic phone extraction and its recipe fixture. Tests shown red first: the upload service (6), the route (11), `AddFiles` (3), the studio's Files stage (2), and `keyboard/add-files.spec.ts` (registry `ADD_FILES_ACTIONS`; the menu case red with its entry switched off). **Not built:** spec 09 §7's extraction profile, and document formats other than plain text (PDF, DOCX, RTF, EML), which need a text reader; both are recorded in spec 09.

## ADR-095 — Extraction uses a real extraction model, reads a whole email, decoded; the Inspector's email list puts emails on the canvas

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as three multiple-choice questions after testing the Enron case: the messages did not go onto the canvas, the reader stopped at 4,000 characters, and *Extract entities* found nothing in an email naming Ken Lay, Portland and the Board of Directors; and the owner's ruling, the same day: "while Enron dataset is for this machine only the features that we discussed should be available across the whole product"). ADR-089 and ADR-092 are unchanged except where this says so.

Context. Four causes, each seen on the owner's deployment, not assumed.

1. **Live extraction ran on the conformance model.** `services/api/app.py` passed `CONFORMANCE_MODEL` (`qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct`) to the email and document extraction services, against `adapters/model_litellm`'s own rule ("this name is conformance-only, never hardcoded into a caller outside `tests/conformance`") and spec 03 §5.2's default (a 7–14B model). Re-run on the owner's email, it returned "Jeff Ken Lay" born 1943-02-16, aliased "Mayor of Portland", four sentences of its own as `Endpoint`s, and "Portland, Oregon"; every item was rightly dropped (confidences on a 0–10 scale read as hundredths, and values not in the text). ADR-020 already says this model is "a poor extractor in absolute terms".
2. **An Enron body was never decoded.** `demo_fixtures/enron.py` read each body with `get_payload(decode=False)`, so quoted-printable stayed encoded: `=20` and soft line breaks (`Ken La= y`) split the very words extraction must find verbatim.
3. **The excerpt was cut at 4,000 characters** (ADR-089 Amendment 1), so the reader and extraction both saw only the start of a long email.
4. **The Inspector's Emails list could not put emails on the canvas** (ADR-092 decision 3 kept the list as a list); the owner opened the emails there, and no Document was written.

Decision.

1. **A deployment's extraction model is its own, chosen by the system administrator on the setup harness's Models screen** (the owner's ruling, the same day: "the LLM selection should be available in the admin harness so that system admin can configure it, use the model that I selected as the default one the product ships with"), written to `osprey.yaml` as `models.extraction`, and never the conformance model. The choice is from a closed list of supported local models, because each must be pinned (ADR-020) before a deployment may pull it; a name off the list is refused by the config's own validation. The list, read from the registry's manifests and checked by the same method against the 0.5B pin:

   | Model | Licence | Download | Manifest digest | |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `qwen2.5:7b-instruct` | Apache-2.0 | 4.68 GB | `845dbda0ea48ed749caafd9e6037047aa19acfcfd82e704d7ca97d631a0b697e` | **the default the product ships with** |
   | `qwen2.5:14b-instruct` | Apache-2.0 | 8.99 GB | `7cdf5a0187d5c58cc5d369b255592f7841d1c4696d45a8c8a9489440385b22f6` | |

   The Conduit's email and document extraction use it; the conformance suite keeps `qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct`. It is pulled and digest-verified by the same script as the others, and the deployment reports healthy only once it is present. Adding a model to the list is adding a row here and its pin.
2. **The model is given room for a whole email, and nothing is cut silently (rule 2).** The extraction model is served with a 32,768-token context. Text longer than one extraction window is read in overlapping windows and the findings joined, each located in the whole text; nothing past a window is dropped unread.
3. **An email is kept whole and decoded.** The Enron loader decodes each body (quoted-printable, base64, the declared character set) and keeps all of it on the event; the reader shows it all and extraction reads it all. `excerpt` keeps its name and now holds the whole body; `truncated` is always false for a new load. The owner reloads the case's events (`--replace-events`).
4. **The Inspector's Emails list has *Put on the canvas***, doing exactly what *Show emails (n)* does from the link menu (ADR-092 decisions 1 and 2: the emails inside the timeline's window, written as Documents, or `limit_exceeded`). Keyboard-reachable (rule 13).
5. **None of this is Enron's alone (the owner's ruling).** Enron is a dataset admitted for this machine only (ADR-053); what it showed is built for every source the product reads:
   - *Decoding*: one shared reader of a message body (`conduit_common/message_text.py`: transfer encoding, character set, the plain-text part of a multipart message) that the Enron loader uses and any email source after it must use; it is not a demo fixture's private code.
   - *Whole text*: the Ingest Studio keeps a recipe's text column whole on its events (phone messages and any other text a recipe marks, ADR-094), and content an entity holds is kept whole; no 4,000-character cut remains on any path that writes text for reading or extraction.
   - *The models*: every model the Conduit uses for analysts' work is the deployment's own, chosen on the Models screen and named in `osprey.yaml`: `models.extraction` (decision 1), `models.vision`, `models.transcription` and `models.embedding`, whose lists hold today's models only (`moondream:1.8b-v2-q4_K_M`, `Systran/faster-whisper-tiny.en`, `all-minilm:22m-l6-v2-fp16`) until the owner chooses others; no production caller names a conformance model. Extraction from a held document, image or video uses the same windows (decision 2).
   - *The canvas*: *Put on the canvas* serves every link whose events carry text, phone messages as well as emails.

Consequences. The deployment downloads 4.68 GB once, and extraction is slower per email than on the 0.5B model. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, each to be shown red first: the Conduit's extraction services are built with the configured models and never a conformance one, checked by a scan of `services/` for a conformance name outside the conformance suite; a Studio recipe's text over 4,000 characters is kept whole on its event; the rendered pull script and LiteLLM config carry the extraction model and its digest, and its context size; a text longer than one window is read in more than one call and a finding from the second window is kept with its locator in the whole text; a quoted-printable Enron body is decoded, and a body over 4,000 characters is kept whole; *Put on the canvas* in the Inspector writes the emails as the menu does, by keyboard.

## ADR-096 — The side panels fold away: an accordion each for the Inspector, the Query builder and Metrics, a preview open, denser type

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (owner, in chat, three messages: "the inspect panel very cluttered with all sorts of options, can you tidy this up and put all options as collapsible menu under accordians"; "Don't put everything into a single accordian, create separate accordians for Inpector, Query Builder and Metrics, only have preview there as default view"; "reduce the font sizes and spacing to make it easy to view and naviate"). The details below are mine, within those asks, and recorded so they can be overruled.

Context. A selected link showed five parts stacked, all open: its details, *Change this link…*, Notes, Emails (with *Put on the canvas*, ADR-095) and Change history. A selected node showed four tabs: Properties, Provenance, Source and Judgements.

Decision.

0. **Each of the three side panels has its own accordion** (ADR-085's column keeps the three panels apart, each movable and sized as before); the parts of one panel fold within it, never into another's. Each opens on its preview, the part read at a glance, and every other part starts folded: the Inspector's *Details* or *Properties* (below), the Query builder's *Pattern* (its nodes, *Preview*, *Run* and what they answer; *Add a pattern variable*, *Connect two pattern nodes*, *Save this pattern* and *Load a saved pattern* fold), and Metrics' *Ranking* (*Communities* and *Filter* fold; more than one may now be open at once).
6. **The style: minimalist and bordered** (the owner's choice, kept when a design review proposed borderless rows; the review's other points taken): one hairline box per part (`--border-subtle`, `--r-control`) with `--sp-4` between, the header a full-width row at `--fs-12` 600 with a chevron on the left that turns when open (no turn under `prefers-reduced-motion`), `--surface-hover` on hover and focus.
5. **Denser type and spacing in the three panels**: the panel title at `--fs-13`, the body and its controls at `--fs-12` with `--lh-12`, and the body's padding and gaps at `--sp-8` and `--sp-4`, from the tokens only; the rest of the Glass is unchanged.
1. **Every part of the Inspector is a section with a header that opens and closes it** (a button with `aria-expanded`, its content a labelled region). A link's sections: *Details*, *Change this link*, *Notes*, the link's events (*Emails (n)*, *Messages (n)* or *Events (n)*) and *Change history*. A node's: *Properties*, *Provenance*, *Source* and *Judgements*, replacing the tabs.
2. **What starts open:** a link's *Details*, a node's *Properties*, and with no node selected *Judgements*; every other section starts closed.
3. **The menus still reach their part.** *Change link…*, *Add a note*, *Show emails (n)* and *Show change history* open their section as well as doing what they did (ADR-080, ADR-075, ADR-089).
4. **A closed section keeps what is in it.** Its content stays in the page, hidden, so a half-written note or change is not lost by closing it, and nothing is fetched again on opening it. Which sections are open lasts for the selection, not across a reload.

Consequences. Spec 02 §2. ADR-070's Metrics strip (closed, one at a time) is replaced; its keyboard id `ranking-section-opens-by-keyboard-and-loads-the-list` becomes `ranking-opens-loaded-and-folds-by-keyboard`, and the Query builder gains `open-a-folded-part-by-keyboard`. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken: each panel opening on its preview with the rest folded (`QueryBuilderPanel.test.tsx`, `MetricsPanel.test.tsx`); a link's sections, which start open and closed, opening and closing by keyboard; a menu hand-over opening its section; a node's sections replacing the tabs, Judgements open with no node; a half-written note surviving its section's closing (`inspector/Inspector.test.tsx`, `keyboard/inspector.spec.ts`, registry `INSPECTOR_ACTIONS`).

## ADR-097 — The design review of 6 October 2026 adopted, against DESIGN.md v0.2, in three steps

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (owner: a usability review of the Glass by Claude Design, sixteen items in priority order, and `spec/design/DESIGN.md` v0.2 placed in the repository; the owner's answer to the five conflicts put to them: "go with your suggestions"). ADR-084, ADR-085, ADR-086 and ADR-096 are unchanged except where this says so.

**DESIGN.md and tokens.css.** `spec/design/DESIGN.md` is the design contract: a value on screen that it does not hold is drift. `apps/workspace/src/design/tokens.css` stays the binding implementation (`CLAUDE.md`), and the two agree, checked: every colour in `tokens.css` is in `DESIGN.md` (its one extra, `#313334`, is named in passing with no role), and the radii match in value under other names (`--r-0` `--r-canvas`, `--r-1` `--r-control`, `--r-2` `--r-panel`, `--r-3` `--r-overlay`, `--r-pill` `--r-chip`). A change to either is made to both. The review asked for `npx impeccable detect`, which is not installed; its place is taken by `tools/colour_drift_check.py`: every colour literal in the Glass's source is one `DESIGN.md` holds, or the file is a declared mirror of the tokens for the WebGL canvas (`color/tokens.ts`, `color/palette.ts`), or it is named in an allowlist with its reason until fixed.

**The five conflicts, decided (the owner, taking my suggestions).**

1. *Right panel (review item 1).* The three panels of ADR-085 stay stacked, movable and sized, each with its ADR-096 accordion; the column becomes the review's right panel (360px by default, resizable as now), with the review's header rows. Not tabs: tabs would hide two of the three.
2. *Reordering (item 8).* *Move up* and *Move down* leave the grip row for a menu on the panel's header, and Alt+↑ and Alt+↓ on a focused header move the panel; dragging stays. The arrows go.
3. *Accordion style (item 14).* The owner's bordered style stays (ADR-096 decision 6) with the review's hairline weight, chevron on the left and `--fs-12` 600 headers.
4. *Case tabs (item 3).* One tab per case, branches as indented child tabs beneath their parent (ADR-084's family); no selection state in any tab label.
5. *Naming (item 15).* The top bar carries the solid-cut mark and the wordmark's chrome short form, **Osprey** (DESIGN.md §2); "Glass" stays the tier's name in the specification and the code, and is not shown.

**The steps.** Each with its spec changes and tests, red first, and keyboard cases (rule 13).

- **Step 1, structure and state (review items 1 to 5 and 16).** A 20px classification strip above everything (the marking of the case open, neutral, `--fs-11` 600 on `--surface-raised`); a 40px top bar (mark, case switcher, search, view switch, the account on the right); a 44px left rail, icons with names on hover and an expandable state, for investigations, branches, history, watches, proposed types and ingest; the canvas toolbar docked at 32px; the timeline collapsed to 32px by default and resizable (ADR-086). One selection bar, bottom centre of the canvas, shown only for a selection: its count, *Expand*, *Branch to a new case*, *Remove from view*, *Clear* (Escape), replacing the three counters; the Inspector's states for one node, several (counts by type, shared properties, the links between them) and none ("Select a node, or press / to search"); brass on the primary action, focus, the selection stroke and the mark only. Done when, measured at 1440×900: no more than three rows of chrome above the canvas, the canvas at least 60% of the height with the timeline collapsed, one live selection counter in the page, and no more than one brass-filled element with nothing focused.
- **Step 2, the canvas (items 9 to 12).** Nodes 20px at 100%; labels `--fs-12`, identifiers in mono, cut in the middle at 24 characters, never past the canvas edge; a zoom cluster with Fit (F); a legend of the types present; the 8px grid (DESIGN.md §9 exception 4); arrowheads, provenance strokes (§3.8) and widths from the sequential scale; the toolbar in labelled groups (Layout, Show) with the display toggles as one segmented control. The performance budget is a CI gate (rule 10) and every one of these costs frame time; `make glass-perf` already fails two cases (FDE handover §4), which are investigated first so this step is judged against a gate that works.
- **Step 3, timeline, Query builder, top bar, accessibility (items 13 to 15 and the checks).** Integer ticks in mono, hours for a single bucket, the mode switch in the header and the rest in an overflow menu; "Community detection" and "Match strictness" named as such; the theme in the account menu; Export as one menu; the brush in tokens; 24px hit targets; the status bar's counts as spaced pairs; reduced motion's instant move with "show previous positions".

### ADR-097, Amendment 1 (6 October 2026) — four things found building step 1

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "go with your suggestions"; recorded so they can be overruled). ADR-097 is unchanged except where this says so.

1. **Review items 6, 7 and 8 belong to step 1.** ADR-097's steps named items 1 to 5 and 16, 9 to 12, and 13 to 15, and left the P1 items 6 (the brush), 7 (button tiers) and 8 (region headers) with no step. They are built in step 1: the brush from the tokens, the quiet tier beside primary and secondary, and the panel headers with their reordering menu.
2. **The case tabs leave their row for the left rail.** Conflict 4's answer kept "one tab per case, branches indented beneath their parent"; review item 1's done-condition allows no more than three rows of chrome above the canvas, and the classification strip, the top bar and the view toolbar are three. So the tabs, unchanged in what they do (ADR-084: open, close, the Branches list, discard), are reached from the rail's *Cases*: the case first, each branch indented beneath it. This is review item 3's own second form ("or an entry in the left rail").
3. **What the classification strip says.** The protective marking of what is on screen: the highest classification among the nodes and links in the view, in the deployment's handling scheme's order, or the scheme's lowest when the view is empty. Not the analyst's clearance, which stays in the account button (ADR-050, ADR-065).
4. **ADR-065's application switch goes; the rest of ADR-065 stands.** Step 1 puts the Ingest Studio on the rail, so a `[Glass | Ingest Studio]` switch in the bar would be a second route to one place and an element the 40px bar has no room for. The rail's *Ingest Studio* opens it; in the Studio the rail holds *Back to the investigation*, which returns to the Glass view last open, as the switch's *Glass* did. ADR-065's brass line under the bar in the Studio, its case and account menus and Filters inside the search box are kept. Watches and History leave the bar for the rail, and the resolution threshold for the Graph's view toolbar.

### ADR-097, Amendment 2 (6 October 2026) — three things decided building step 2's links

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "go with your suggestions"; recorded so they can be overruled). ADR-081 and ADR-097 are unchanged except where this says so.

1. **Provenance comes before basis.** DESIGN.md §3.8 strokes a link by provenance and ADR-081 by basis, and the two can disagree (an inferred link of a Direct type). An inferred link is dashed whatever its basis, because "a model said this and no person has confirmed it" (rule 5) is the more consequential thing to see, and it stops being true the moment someone confirms it, when the basis shows again; an unresolved link is dotted; an asserted link is drawn by its basis. A Probabilistic asserted link and an unresolved one therefore look alike, which I accept: both say "do not take this as established".
2. **§3.8's patterns are scaled for the canvas.** `4 2` and `1 2` are written for a one-pixel SVG stroke; on the WebGL canvas a gap of two pixels or less rasterises away and the line reads as solid grey. The dash is drawn eight on, four off (`4 2` doubled), and the dot keeps ADR-081's three on, four off. DESIGN.md is not edited; this is the record of the difference.
3. **Weight as width stops at 10,000 links in view.** Widths from the sequential scale need the program that honours width; on 250,000 links that took the perf gate's first frame from 8.7s to 17.0s (measured both ways). Above 10,000 links in view, an undeclared link is one pixel on the line program; the strength filter still orders links by weight there. A declared thickness (ADR-081) is always honoured.

## ADR-098 — Links among what is on screen; a fast recogniser first and the model on request; asking the model about chosen documents in a branch; an entity marked by hand

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as multiple-choice questions after testing the redesigned Glass on Enron: "it doesn't show the communication between the email addresses that have been placed on the screen", answered "Both automatic and on demand"; "would it be better to plug in the Stanford NLP for quick extraction of the POLE entities and keep LLM for more detailed extraction", answered Stanza and "Option 1, but with the UX for requesting LLM as well. Also allow for a set of documents to be selected on the canvas for LLM analysis in a new branch"; and "the ability for the analyst to highlight and designate an entity from a document"). ADR-084, ADR-089, ADR-092, ADR-094 and ADR-095 are unchanged except where this says so.

Context. An expansion returns only the links it walked along (`ExpandBuilder.render_edges_gremlin`: the seed's own edges), so after expanding a person the canvas shows a star; a link between two of the addresses now on screen is never asked for, and degrees of separation between them cannot be seen. Extraction runs the 7B model over each email (ADR-095), which is thorough and slow, and it mistypes plain places (Houston and Portland proposed as Endpoints). Stanford CoreNLP was asked for by name; it is GPL-3.0, which `make licence-check` rejects (`00_ARCHITECTURE.md` licence register), so the Stanford NLP group's Apache-2.0 library, Stanza, is used instead.

Decision.

1. **Links among a set of nodes.** `GraphPort.edges_among(node_ids, principal, edge_types=None)` returns every edge whose two ends are both in the set, with access control in the adapter on the edge and on both ends (rule 3): an edge the principal may not see, or one whose other end they may not see, leaves no trace, not in a count either. `POST /v1/investigations/{id}/links-among` with `node_ids` (or none, for every node in the view) adds those not already in the view to the working set and answers with the delta; it counts first, and past the working set's cap it adds nothing and answers the typed `limit_exceeded` with its three options (rule 2). **Automatic:** an expansion that adds at most 100 new nodes, into a view of at most 2,000 nodes, also brings the links among its new nodes and every node already in the view, under the same cap. **On demand:** *Show links among these* on the selection bar (the selected nodes) and in the canvas toolbar's View group (everything in view), for larger views and for links the analyst wants to see now.
2. **A fast recogniser first.** *Extract entities* runs Stanza's English named-entity recogniser (Apache-2.0) in a sidecar of its own, beside the transcription one, behind a new `RecognisePort` with a conformance suite written first (rule 1). Its types map to the ontology: PERSON to Person, ORG to Organisation, GPE, LOC and FAC to Location; an email address and a phone number found by pattern to Endpoint; other types (dates, money) are not proposed. Its findings are suggestions in the same review list, inferred until accepted (rule 5), with the recogniser named as their source. The model's pinned weights are downloaded once at deployment, as the language models are.
3. **The language model on request.** Beside *Extract entities*, *Ask the model to extract* runs the ADR-095 extraction (the deployment's extraction model) on the same email or Document, for the entities, relationships and patterns the recogniser cannot find; its findings join the same list.
4. **Asking the model about chosen documents, in a branch.** With Documents selected on the canvas, the selection bar offers *Ask the model about these…*. It branches the selection into a new case (ADR-084), named "Questions on <n> documents", and opens a conversation in that branch: the analyst asks, the model answers from those documents' text only, citing which document each point comes from, and anything it proposes (an entity, a link, a pattern) is listed with *Accept* and *Reject*, inferred until accepted, and accepted into the branch's canvas. The conversation is kept with the branch, audited, and only to those who can see it.
5. **An entity marked by hand.** In the reader, selecting words in a document's text offers *Mark as…* with the ontology's entity types: the analyst's designation is written as a node of that type with a `MENTIONED_IN` link to the document, its source the document with the selection's locator and excerpt hash. It is asserted, not inferred, because a person made it; it is attributed to them.

Order of building: 1, then 5, then 2 and 3 together, then 4.

Consequences. A sidecar image with Stanza and a CPU build of its runtime, about 1.5 GB, and an English model of about 200 MB downloaded once; licence register entries for each. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, each shown red first: a hidden edge between two visible nodes, and an edge to a hidden node, are absent from `edges_among` for an unauthorised principal and present for a cleared one; `links-among` past the cap adds nothing and answers `limit_exceeded`; a small expansion brings the links among its new nodes and the view, and a large one does not; the recogniser's conformance suite proves its type mapping and that it proposes nothing as accepted; a branch's conversation is refused to an analyst who cannot see the branch; a designation by hand is written with the selection's locator and attributed to the analyst.

### ADR-098, Amendment 1 (6 October 2026) — what building decision 2 found

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "go ahead with the builds"; recorded so they can be overruled). ADR-098 is unchanged except where this says so.

1. **Stanza is held at 1.10.1.** Every release from 1.11.0 to 1.15.0 requires `udtools` (GPL-2.0-or-later), and with it `udapi` (GPL-3.0-or-later); the licence register rejects both (`00_ARCHITECTURE.md` §7). 1.10.1 is the last release without them and its English recogniser does the work decision 2 asks for. Moving past it needs those two packages gone from Stanza's requirements, or a recorded exception, not a version bump.
2. **The recogniser image checks its own licences at build.** `make licence-check` reads the Conduit's Python environment and cannot see a sidecar's, so `services/ner/licence_gate.py` applies the same rule inside the image and fails the build on any GPL licence and on any it cannot read. The first version used a list of licences to refuse and passed both GPL packages: pip-licenses 5.0.0 reports their `License-Expression` metadata as `UNKNOWN`, which no refusal list matches. It is default-deny now, on pip-licenses 5.5.5, which reads them; `tests/test_ner_licence_gate.py` keeps its allowlist identical to the repository's.
3. **A recogniser finding carries no score.** Stanza gives none; the finding's `confidence` is 1.0 and means only "found", and the reader and the Inspector say *found by Stanza* in place of a percentage. A hand-marking (decision 5) says *marked by hand*.
4. **The routes default to the recogniser; the services to the model.** A caller that names nothing (`using` left out) gets the fast pass, as decision 2 says; the services' own default stays the model so a caller inside the Conduit that predates this keeps its behaviour.

### ADR-098, Amendment 2 (7 October 2026) — what building decision 4 found

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "go ahead with the builds"; recorded so they can be overruled). ADR-098 is unchanged except where this says so.

1. **The model proposes entities; links and patterns are in its answer.** Decision 4 lists "an entity, a link, a pattern" as things the model may propose. This build proposes entities only (Person, Organisation, Location, Endpoint), each placed by the exact words the model quotes from the Document it names, and accepted as an inferred node with a `MENTIONED_IN` link to that Document, the same shape as an extraction's finding. Who wrote to whom, when and about what is described in the answer, citing the Documents. A proposed link between two entities would need its own review record (no store holds a pending edge today) and a way to show what it rests on; that is left for a decision of its own, not filled in here.
2. **What the model reads, and the limit.** The model reads every Document in the case's view that the asker can see (`WorkingSetService.visible_membership`, the handling filter of every read), whole, numbered, never a Document above the asker. Together they may come to at most 80,000 characters, so that the instructions, question and answer fit the extraction model's 32,768-token context (ADR-095). Past that the question is refused (413, `documents_too_large`, with both figures), never cut and answered in part (rule 2). A case with no Document the asker can see is refused (422, `no_documents`).
3. **A proposal is placed or counted, never guessed.** The model's quote (or failing that, the name) is looked for in the named Document's text; found, the finding carries the Dossier's `char span {start}-{end}` locator and its excerpt hash; not found, or naming no Document of the case, it is left out and the answer says how many were (`unplaced`).
4. **The conversation is the case's, and shown as far as each reader can see.** Questions are kept in Postgres (`case_questions`), audited (`ask_question`, `accept_question_candidate`, `reject_question_candidate`), asked at Editor and read at Viewer. The answer's words may come from any Document the model read, so each question keeps the Documents it was read over (`read_ids`), and a reader who cannot see every one of them is not shown that question at all, nor told that one was left out, which would say that a Document above them is in the case (rule 3). Found while writing this amendment: the first version showed every reader the answer and filtered only its citations. A reader shown the question sees its citations and its proposals as their unit's review records allow.
5. **Tests:** `tests/services/api/test_questions.py` (the hidden Document never sent to the model, an answer read over a Document the reader cannot see not shown to them, refusal past the limit, placement and the unplaced count, accept and reject), `test_questions_store.py` on real Postgres, the levels table, `QuestionsPanel.test.tsx`, `keyboard/questions.spec.ts` and the selection bar case in `keyboard/selection.spec.ts`.

### ADR-098, Amendment 3 (9 October 2026) — the two passes named for what they do, and a pending finding shown where it sits

Status: accepted 9 October 2026 (the owner's choice between presented options: "Quick scan + deeper read" and "all pending, on listing"). ADR-098 is unchanged except where this says so.

The owner, on the reader: "the option for Extract Entities vs Ask Model to extract is very confusing", and asked for the found words to be marked in the content itself. What was confusing, precisely: *Extract entities* disappeared once findings were listed, while *Ask the model to extract* sat beside it styled so quietly it read as plain text — a pair that looked like one action and a caption rather than two actions.

1. **The two passes are equal buttons, always offered, named for what they do**: *Quick scan* (the recogniser) and *Deep read (model)*, in the reader with a caption under each ("Names, emails and numbers, in seconds"; "A slower, deeper read; findings are added") and in the Inspector's narrow events panel with the same words as tooltips. Neither disappears; both disable while a pass runs, with an "Extracting…" status line. The wire shape (`using: recogniser | model`) is unchanged.
2. **A pending finding is shown where it sits in the text, as soon as it is listed.** Each candidate's `char span` locator and `excerpt_hash` (already in the API's candidate record) are read by the Glass; the words at the locator's place are marked only when they hash to the candidate's own excerpt hash — the server's "a locator never points at something else" check, made again where the marking happens. Pending findings draw dashed (the inferred visual language, rule 5), are not clickable (there is no node yet), and an accepted span always wins overlapping words. A finding whose span fails the check, falls beyond the shown text (the reader shows the first 4,000 characters), or overlaps an earlier one keeps its list row and simply is not marked.
3. **Tests:** `pendingSpans.test.ts` (placed only where the words hash right; beyond-text, accepted and unlocated dropped; overlap keeps the first), `DocumentReader.test.tsx` (both buttons offered as equals with their captions, still offered after findings list, a pending finding marked in place — all three red first), the renamed keyboard cases in `reader.spec.ts` and `link-events.spec.ts`.

## ADR-099 — A case sees only its own datasets, on every read, as a limit of access

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (the owner's two choices, put as multiple-choice questions after "the search seems to find data from all dataset / cases when the search should be restricted to the dataset selected": *every read* over search only or the view only, and *a hard limit* over a working filter). ADR-050, ADR-052 and ADR-084 are unchanged except where this says so. Built in four steps; until step 2 is built every read is as before.

### Context: what was seen

Searching `vol` in the Fixture Corp case suggested `volume.management@enron.com`. Nothing was wrong with the route: `/v1/search` and `/v1/suggest` say they are "not investigation-scoped" (`services/api/search.py`), a case is a view of one shared graph, and nothing records which data a case is about. Expansion, the query builder and the links-among routes read the same graph the same way, so an Enron neighbour could join a Fixture Corp view by expansion too. The graph knows where each element came from only in its provenance (`enron-corpus`, `fixture-corp`) or its Studio `load_id`.

### Decision

1. **A dataset is a named body of data held by a unit.** The Enron corpus, Fixture Corp, the scenarios, PaySim, HMP and each body of data loaded through the Ingest Studio is one. A dataset has an id, a name and an owning unit, and is kept in the Conduit (`datasets`, Postgres).
2. **Every node and link carries the datasets it belongs to** (`datasets`, a list, stored as an indexed top-level field beside the handling fields). A write names its dataset; writing an element that already exists adds the dataset to the ones it has (a union, as provenance is merged), never replaces them. One person or address seen in two datasets stays one node (rule 6), visible to a case of either; its links stay with the dataset that wrote them. Its properties are the latest write's, as today: an analyst of either case reads them. Keeping properties apart per dataset is not built and would need its own decision.
3. **A case names its datasets**, at least one, all of its own unit. A branch takes its parent's. Changing them is the case's Author's, audited, and refused for a dataset of another unit; nothing else widens them.
4. **The read is limited in the store, like handling (rule 3).** The case's datasets ride with the principal (`Principal.datasets`), and the graph adapter adds `filter(values("datasets").unfold().is(within(...)))` to the one access step every read already builds (`AccessFilter.gremlin_has_step`). Not `has("datasets", within(...))`: on ArcadeDB 25.5.1 that compares the whole list with each value and matches nothing, measured on a throwaway server, so a case would see no data and a test of refusals alone would pass. The step applies so node, link and the far end of each link are all limited, in search, suggestions, `get_node`, `find_node`, expansion, paths, `match` and its count, `edges_among`, `neighbourhood_stats` and `list_nodes`. A node outside the case's datasets cannot be detected by any count, degree, path length or bucket: the conformance suite gets a dataset section modelled on its handling one. `expand_candidate_count`, the unfiltered half of `filtered_count`, takes the case's datasets too: what lies outside a case's datasets is not "hidden" from it, it is not in its world, and counting it would say there is more.
5. **A principal outside a case sees no data.** The Conduit's principal for a request whose path names a case carries that case's datasets; for any other request it carries none, and a read with none returns nothing (default-deny, as an unrecognised clearance sees nothing). So search, suggestions and the query builder move under the case (`/v1/investigations/{id}/search`, `.../suggest`, `.../patterns/preview`, `.../patterns/run`, Viewer) and the unscoped routes go. Only the Conduit's own background work (resolution, a load's lookups, seeding) reads unlimited (`datasets=None`), and no request handler can make that principal.
6. **Data added to a case joins one of its datasets**: the first, unless the load names another of the case's. A Studio load, a file added, an extraction accepted, a hand-marking and an accepted question proposal each write with it.
7. **Events are already the case's.** The analytics store keys each event to the case it was loaded into (`investigation_scope`, with branches inheriting their parent's links' events, `services/api/event_scope.py`), and per-link reads are gated by the link's visibility, which step 2 limits. No dataset column is added there.

### Steps

1. The store: `datasets` on writes and on what is read back, the union on upsert and bulk load, the index, the access step, `expand_candidate_count`; the conformance section, written first (rule 1).
2. The Conduit: the `datasets` and `investigation_datasets` tables, the case's datasets on create, branch and change (audited), the scoped principal, the routes moved under the case and the unscoped ones removed, an access test on each (rule 4).
3. The data: each seed and Studio load writes its dataset; `python -m scripts.stamp_datasets` stamps what is already stored from its provenance (`enron-corpus`, `fixture-corp`, …) and names the existing cases' datasets, so the owner's deployment needs no re-seed.
4. The Glass: a new case chooses its datasets, the case list and the top bar name them, the Author changes them, search and the query builder call the case's routes.

### Cost

Every read gains one `within` step on an indexed field. Every write path must name a dataset, so each is touched once. A case that should see two bodies of data must name both, and an analyst looking for links across datasets must make a case over both: that is the limit the owner chose.

### ADR-099, Amendment 1 (7 October 2026) — what building step 2 found

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "carry on with all four steps"; recorded so they can be overruled). ADR-099 is unchanged except where this says so.

1. **The scope is in `get_principal`, not beside it.** Every principal a route is given comes from `get_principal`, the Studio's role checks included (`require_studio_role` takes `PrincipalDep`), so scoping there limits every route at once: the datasets of the case its path names, none for any other path. A dependency beside it would have missed the Studio load, which runs in the request under a role principal. A test that overrides `get_principal` gets an unlimited principal, as before this ADR; the scoping itself is tested through the real dependency (`tests/services/api/test_dataset_scope.py`).
2. **The Conduit's own writes are stamped at one point.** The services write through `DatasetStampingGraph`, which gives any write naming no dataset the first of the request's case's datasets (held in a context variable set by `get_principal`). A write that names datasets keeps them; outside a request nothing is stamped. Without it a marked entity, an accepted finding or a file added would have vanished from its case as it was written.
3. **The working set's own projection applies the axis too.** The delta stream and a reconnect re-project stored bodies without a graph read (`WorkingSetService._project`), so `ontology.handling.principal_may_read` adds the datasets to the handling check there. The stream's principal comes from a ticket minted outside any case; the stream scopes it to its own case.
4. **Not every graph-reading route moved.** Search, suggestions, the query builder's preview and run, paths, and confirm, retract and the suppression mark on a node name no case, so they moved under `/v1/investigations/{id}/` (Viewer to read; Editor for the three that write). The analytics routes already name their case in the body and read the analytics store, which is case-keyed (decision 7), so they stay. An alert is read as the case it arose in reads (an alert with none reads nothing of its entities), and a case opened from an alert takes that case's datasets, or a new dataset of its own.
5. **A load's lookups stay within the case.** The Studio's `on_match: reference` lookup reads with the case's principal, so a value already held only by another dataset is not found and a new node is made for it in this dataset. That follows the hard limit; it means one address loaded into two datasets by two loads is two nodes, joined only by resolution, unless the loads write the same node id (as the seeds do).
6. **Export of a link** still checks the link's handling as the client submitted it (`services/api/export.py`'s disclosed limit, there being no `get_edge`); its datasets are not checked there. A client can only submit a link it was shown, which the case's reads have already limited.

### ADR-099, Amendment 2 (7 October 2026) — what building step 3 found

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "carry on with all four steps"; recorded so they can be overruled). ADR-099 is unchanged except where this says so.

1. **The seeds name their datasets** (`demo_fixtures/datasets.py`: Enron, Fixture Corp, HMP, PaySim, the acceptance scenarios). Each seed writes through `DatasetStampingGraph(..., dataset=...)`, so everything it loads is in its dataset whichever write path it takes, and the case it makes, or is told to load into, reads that dataset (`case_seed.ensure_case_reads`, required by `case_from_arguments` and `scope_for`). A dataset of that id held by another unit is refused, never borrowed.
2. **A correction keeps its datasets.** `supersede_node` and `supersede_edge` give the new revision every dataset of the old one, and a link cloned onto a corrected node keeps its own. Found by the conformance case written for it: confirming a node in a case made it vanish from the case, since the replacement is built by its caller naming no dataset.
3. **A `SAME_AS` link is in the datasets both its records share.** Two records are resolved together only inside a body of data holding both; a match across two datasets is in none, so no case reads it and neither case's records are joined to the other's (`services/resolve/same_as_writer.py`). Resolution itself still compares across the corpus; only what it writes is limited.
4. **What is already stored is stamped, not re-seeded:** `python -m scripts.stamp_datasets` (`--dry-run` first). It stamps what each seed loaded by its provenance source; gives each case that reads nothing its datasets (the seeds whose load id names it or whose case name it bears, what is on its canvas, its parent's; else one of its own, named after it); stamps what an analyst wrote onto a canvas before ADR-099 with the case's first dataset; and rewrites the working set's copies, from which the canvas is drawn. It ends by counting, per type, what is still in no dataset: no case reads those until something claims them. Two ArcadeDB 25.5.1 facts it rests on, both measured: `datasets.append(x)` turns the list into a string (`'[fixture-corp]enron'`) and there is no `union()`, so it sets a missing list and appends with `||`; and "in no dataset" is `datasets IS NULL OR datasets.size() = 0`, since an element written since ADR-099 naming none holds an empty list, which `IS NULL` misses.
5. **Not covered:** a history step recorded before ADR-099 holds bodies with no datasets, and restoring it (`WorkingSetService.restore`, which re-projects the stored bodies) shows none of them. Restoring a step re-read from the graph would fix it; not built.

### ADR-099, Amendment 3 (7 October 2026) — every Glass feature within the dataset; types the one exception

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (the owner's ruling: "the scope of Glass features should be restricted to the dataset scope only. The only exception being the link type and entity types that are declared at a global dataset level, i.e., the OspreyFlow default dataset that is only available to admin users"; and three multiple-choice answers: a type an analyst defines lives *in that dataset*; saved patterns, watches and Studio recipes are scoped *all of them*; the deployment's data restored now). ADR-090 and ADR-099 are unchanged except where this says so.

1. **The OspreyFlow default dataset holds the types, and only the types.** The ontology in force at its global level (`default.yaml` and every promoted type) is read by every case and changed only by an administrator (promote, rename, retire; ADR-090). It holds no nodes or links, and no case reads data through it.
2. **A type an analyst defines belongs to the dataset of the case it was defined in.** Today that is a link type proposed from the change form (ADR-090): usable at once in every case reading that dataset, offered and drawn nowhere else, and promoted into the default dataset only by an administrator, after which every case has it. This replaces ADR-090's "usable in that case, its branches, and any case where one of its links is in view". Analysts have no way to define an entity type today; when one is built, the same rule holds.
3. **Saved patterns, watches and Studio recipes belong to a dataset.** A saved pattern, a hotlist, a monitor (and the alerts it raises) and an Ingest Studio recipe or source file belongs to the first dataset of the case it was made in; it is listed, offered, evaluated and run only in cases reading that dataset, and its routes move under the case. A watch raises an alert only on data of its dataset.
4. **What already exists keeps working, inside the limit.** A record made before this amendment names no case. It is given the dataset of the case it was made in where that is recorded (an alert's case, a recipe's loads); otherwise a copy of it is given to each dataset its owner's cases read, which widens nothing, since a pattern, a hotlist identifier or a recipe holds no data of its own, and each copy is then evaluated only within its dataset.
5. **Steps.** (a) link-type proposals by dataset; (b) saved patterns; (c) watches; (d) Studio recipes and source files; (e) the existing records, by `scripts.stamp_datasets`. Each with its conformance or store test first and an access test on every read path (rules 1, 4).

## ADR-100 — Starting points for an analyst new to a dataset: an Explore panel

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (the owner: "if the analyst does not have background about a dataset this causes a challenge since they would not know what to start searching for. Can you propose some ideas"; eight ideas put to them, all four groups chosen, *empty canvas and rail* for where). Built after ADR-099 Amendment 3. ADR-099 is unchanged.

### Decision

1. **An *Explore* panel**, shown in the canvas while the view is empty and always reachable as *Explore* on the left rail, for the case it is opened in. Everything in it is read within the case's datasets and the analyst's clearance, and anything in it puts what it names on the canvas (or, for a time, the timeline's window) with one action.
2. **What the dataset holds:** the count of each entity type and each link type, and the time its events span (first and last).
3. **Most connected:** the 10 nodes with the most links. Broadcast addresses (a mailing list writing to hundreds) can be left out, by a threshold of recipients per message shown with the list.
4. **Browse by entity type:** each type with its count and its 5 most connected members, opening to every member, paged and sorted by connections.
5. **Busiest links and moments:** the pairs with the most messages between them, and the days with the most events.
6. **Groups and bridges:** the largest communities with each one's most central member, and the nodes joining otherwise separate groups.
7. **What is new:** the latest loads into the dataset, and entities colleagues confirmed or marked in it recently.
8. **Starter questions:** a short list of query-builder patterns that suit the dataset's types (people who wrote to two of the same people; addresses sharing a name), each run with one action.

### Constraints it is built to

- **Every count and ranking is the analyst's own** (rules 3 and 7). Counts, degrees and rankings are computed in the store with the access step every read uses, so a node the analyst cannot see is never counted, ranked or named. Where a ranking is precomputed for speed it is kept per dataset and per handling class, never once for everyone and filtered afterwards.
- **Cost.** Ranking 234,000 Enron links on each opening is too slow, so the rankings are computed after each load into a dataset and kept; the panel says when they were computed.
- **Nothing is truncated silently** (rule 2): a "top 10" says it is the top 10 of how many, and the browse list pages rather than stops.
- **Keyboard** (rule 13): every item is reachable and actionable by keyboard, with its own case in a keyboard spec.

### ADR-099, Amendment 4 (7 October 2026) — what building Amendment 3's parts (b) to (d) decided

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "go ahead with all five parts of Amendment 3"; recorded so they can be overruled). ADR-099 Amendment 3 is unchanged except where this says so.

1. **A monitor watches its saved pattern's dataset**, not only the first of the case's: a case reading two datasets could otherwise make a monitor in one for a pattern in the other, which would stop at its first evaluation.
2. **A hotlist's match in another dataset writes nothing at all**, not even the `notify` stub ADR-038 writes for a match its owner cannot see: the stub would say that something matched there, which is outside the case's world, not hidden within it.
3. **A case opened from an alert reads the alert's dataset**, else what the alert's case reads, else a dataset of its own.
4. **Source files are kept in flat folders named for their dataset**: an upload made in a case lands in `uploaded/<dataset>/`, an operator may drop a dataset's files in `<root>/<dataset>/`, and a case's listing offers its datasets' folders, each still one directory with nothing below it. The files directly in the root and in `uploaded/`, placed before this amendment, are offered to every case and marked as in no dataset, until an operator moves one into a dataset's folder: a raw file is not yet any dataset's data, and everything a load writes from it is stamped with the loading case's dataset. A dataset id that is not a plain folder name is never joined onto a path.
5. **The Ingest Studio works only within a case**: with none open it says so rather than calling routes that now belong to one. The connector and transform catalogues stay global; they describe the system, not data.
6. **The authorised-query gate reads a query built as an f-string**, which joining a dataset clause onto a query makes it, by its literal parts; a query that binds no principal is still flagged (shown both ways).


### ADR-099, Amendment 5 (7 October 2026) — part (e): records made before Amendment 3 are placed where their case says, and otherwise left as they were

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "go ahead with all five parts of Amendment 3"; recorded so it can be overruled). It departs from Amendment 3 decision 4's "a copy of it is given to each dataset its owner's cases read".

1. **A link-type proposal or an alert takes the first dataset of the case it records** (`scripts.stamp_datasets` step 6, `place_records`); one whose case reads no dataset yet is left and counted.
2. **A saved pattern, hotlist, monitor or Studio recipe made before Amendment 3 is not copied.** None of them records a case, so a copy per dataset would be a guess multiplied: a monitor copied into every dataset raises alerts in each, and a recipe copied twice would publish into a dataset it was never meant for. Each stays, naming no dataset, readable in every case of its owner (`reach_clause`'s legacy branch), and the script counts them per table so the owner can see what is left. Copying, if wanted, is a choice an analyst makes in the case, not one a script makes for them.
3. **What it rests on, measured:** the owner's deployment held none of these records when this was written (link_type_proposals, saved_patterns, hotlists, monitors, alerts and studio_recipes all 0), so nothing is lost by not copying there. A deployment whose tables do not yet have the `dataset_id` column (the Conduit adds it at start-up) is told so per table, not failed.
4. **Tests:** `tests/test_stamp_records.py`, against real Postgres: the case's first dataset is taken (red with the last planted instead), a record with no case is counted and not placed, a dry run writes nothing (red with the write guard removed), a second run moves nothing.

## ADR-101 — ArcadeDB 26.10.1: an update no longer hides other records from an index

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (the owner, offered a workaround on 25.5.1 or the upgrade, chose "Upgrade to 26.10.1 now"). Supersedes the pin of `05_DEPLOYMENT.md` §8 ("ArcadeDB 25.5.1, now the pinned version"); nothing else there changes.

### Context

Found building ADR-100's conformance cases: a read of one entity type found none of its nodes once one of them had been reverted. Measured in plain SQL over HTTP, with none of this repository's code: on ArcadeDB 25.5.1, three records share a value under a `NOTUNIQUE` index, one record's value changes, and a lookup of that value finds **0** of the other 2; a scan finds 2, and `REBUILD INDEX` restores the lookup. The same three steps on 26.10.1 find 2. Every in-place change of an indexed value triggers it: a revert (`reverted`), a re-write with new handling, an edited property. Every read whose entry point is a type and an indexed value is affected: `list_nodes` (resolution's corpus read), search and suggestions, the type-filtered Explore reads, and `scripts.stamp_datasets`' SQL. The owner's deployment already disagreed with itself with no revert ever made, read-only and measured: `PRESENT_AT` 610 links by scan, 606 by index; `COMMUNICATED_WITH` 49,501 and 49,500.

### Decision

1. **The pin is `arcadedata/arcadedb:26.10.1`** in `harness/render.py` (the rendered deployment) and `deploy/compose/dev.yaml`. The owner's `Makefile` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` carry the old tag and are changed by the owner (lines named in the friction log).
2. **Gremlin runs on 26.10.1's Groovy engine** (`-Darcadedb.gremlin.engine=groovy`). Its default parser, TinkerPop's grammar, refuses bound variables (`within(ids)`) and closures, which the edge writes and the bulk loader are built from; 25.5.1 was already running them as Groovy, so the posture does not change. 26.10.1 runs Groovy over HTTP only for `root` (security advisory GHSA-h2j4-28h8-cj5v), which is the user the adapter connects as. Rewriting the adapter's Gremlin for the grammar parser, so the setting can go, is recorded as future work, not done.
3. **The client reads 26's map results as 25.5.1's** (`client._gremlin_row`): a map arrives as `{"result": [{"key", "value"}, ...]}`, and `elementMap()` lists the record id before the `id` property, so a later entry wins, as it did.
4. **A store moved from 25.5.1 is upgraded in place and its indexes rebuilt.** ArcadeDB converts the files on first open; `REBUILD INDEX *` then repairs what 25.5.1 lost. A backup is taken first: a minor-version downgrade needs an export and re-import, not the old image.

### Tests

- `tests/conformance/graph_port/test_suite.py`: reverting, correcting and re-writing one of three nodes leaves the others listed (the revert case red on 25.5.1, all green on 26.10.1). The whole graph conformance suite on 26.10.1: 116 of 117 pass, the one failure the golden-text case that fails on 25.5.1 too.
- `tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_client_map_results.py`: the entry shape, nested maps, scalars left alone, the `id` property over the record id (red with the first entry winning).
- `tests/harness/test_render.py::test_arcadedb_is_a_version_whose_indexes_survive_an_update_and_runs_our_gremlin` (red on the old render).
- The ArcadeDB-backed adapter, seed, stamping, resolution and ingest tests on 26.10.1: 205 pass; 8 fail for want of MinIO, as they do on 25.5.1.

### Not measured

26.10.1's memory over a sustained load (`05_DEPLOYMENT.md` §8 was measured on 25.5.1); its refusal of a write computed from a stale read (a retryable `ConcurrentModificationException`, new in 26.10.1), which no case here exercises under concurrent writers; the upgrade of the owner's deployment itself, done after the Enron reload with their agreement.

### ADR-101, Amendment 1 (7 October 2026) — what upgrading a kept store found

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "Upgrade first, then reload").

1. **The image's user changed**: 25.5.1 runs as uid 1001, 26.10.1 as 1000. A store moved with its volumes kept has them handed to 1000 first (`chown -R 1000:1000`, in a one-off container), or the server stops at start, before opening a database. Refresh does not do this; a future pin move that changes the user needs the same step.
2. **The image has no `curl`**: the probe is busybox `wget` (`harness/render.py`, `deploy/compose/dev.yaml`), and refresh carries a moved service's probe with its image.
3. **The config volume takes the new release's defaults**: of the eight files a 25.5.1 store holds, seven were its untouched defaults and are replaced with 26.10.1's; `server-users.jsonl` (the root user) is kept, as ArcadeDB's upgrade notes say.
4. **`REBUILD INDEX *` after the move** repaired the owner's indexes: every type agrees with a scan. 26.10.1 also discarded the record counts 25.5.1 cached, which it says could be wrong.
5. **A store moved from 25.5.1 is checked before its indexes are rebuilt.** 25.5.1's broken unique indexes let duplicate ids in (on the owner's store, 22 links a replayed commit wrote twice); `REBUILD INDEX *` then drops a unique index it cannot build again, and the Conduit cannot start. The order is: `CHECK DATABASE`; remove duplicates by id (never by record id alone: the two copies can share a stored chunk, and deleting one breaks both, as it did here) or with `CHECK DATABASE FIX`; `CHECK DATABASE` to 0 errors; then `REBUILD INDEX *`.

### ADR-100, Amendment 1 (7 October 2026) — stage 1: the store's two reads

Status: accepted 7 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "carry on with ADR-100"; recorded so it can be overruled). ADR-100 is unchanged except where this says so.

1. **Two `GraphPort` reads**, the panel's sources for decisions 2 to 4: `type_counts(principal)` (nodes per entity type, links per link type) and `most_connected(principal, *, entity_type=None, limit=10, offset=0)` (nodes by degree, most first, ties by id, with `total` and `offset`). Types in `schemas/explore.py`.
2. **Every figure is the principal's own, in the traversal** (rule 3): the access step on each node, each link and each link's other end. A link counts, in a type count and in a degree, only when both its ends can be seen; reverted and superseded elements and other datasets count nowhere. The conformance cases check each twice: right on its own, and unchanged once hidden, other-dataset and reverted neighbours are added beside it.
3. **A ranking says of how many** (rule 2): `total` is the number of nodes ranked, and a page past the end is empty, never a short page that looks whole.
4. **Computed live for now.** ADR-100's cost constraint (rankings kept per dataset and handling class, recomputed after a load) is not built: whether a live ranking is fast enough is measured on the reloaded Enron case first, and the store kept only if it is not.

### ADR-100, Amendment 2 (8 October 2026) — stage 3: the panel in the Glass

Status: accepted 8 October 2026 (mine, within the owner's "carry on with stage 3, the Glass panel"; recorded so it can be overruled).

1. **Decisions 2 to 4 are built** (`spec/02_GLASS_FRONTEND.md`, "Where to start in a case's data"): over an empty canvas as *Where to start*, and from the rail as *Explore*. Decisions 5 to 8 (busiest links and days, groups and bridges, what is new, starter questions) are not built; each needs its own store read and conformance cases first.
2. **A pick is a search result's choice**: drawn, drawn outwards three links (ADR-070, with its large-expansion prompt) and selected, so a hub of thousands asks before it draws, exactly as searching it would.
3. **Pages ask for what is left**: *Show n more* asks for at most 10 and says how many; the panel never asks for, or shows, more than the ranking holds.
4. **Not measured yet:** how long `most_connected` takes on the Enron case live (ADR-100 Amendment 1, decision 4). The panel says *Counting…* while it waits; whether the rankings must be kept per dataset is decided on that measurement.

### ADR-052, Amendment 11 (8 October 2026) — a published ADR no longer leans on a private one

Status: accepted 8 October 2026 (the owner: "align these decision logs as needed and supersede the stale one").

Amendment 6 item 4 says the 405 on the case list was "fixed by the refresh sequence (ADR-049 Amendment)". ADR-049 is a process record and is not published with the product, so a published reader cannot follow that reference. It is superseded by this: the fix is the refresh sequence, `make refresh` (`python -m scripts.refresh`, `05_DEPLOYMENT.md` §3), which rebuilds the owned images and brings the deployment up to date. Nothing else in Amendment 6 changes. The decision-log publication gate now reads an amendment as its own ADR's (`tools/decision_log_publication_check.py`), which is how this citation was found: it had been read as ADR-055's, under whose heading ADR-049's own amendments stand.

### ADR-052, Amendment 12 (11 October 2026) — the Share panel, and a grantee is named by account id

Status: accepted 11 October 2026 (the owner, asked how a dashboard identity is to be given Viewer on a case when no screen for it existed: "Build the Share panel").

1. **The Share panel is built** — decision 9's last unbuilt piece. "Who can open this case" sits in the Cases drawer under "Data this case reads". Everyone holding `share_case` (ADR-112) sees their own level; the case's Author sees every account holding a level, gives an account a level (Viewer, Editor or Author) and removes one. An account without `share_case` is answered 403 by `GET …/access` and the panel is not shown at all. The panel never offers to remove the case's last Author (the store does not refuse it; the administrator's safety net of decision 4 would still reach the case, but the panel does not invite the stranding). It enforces nothing: the Conduit decides every change, and a refusal is said in words.
2. **A grantee is named by account id, not account name — a correction of fact to P3.** P3 and `03_CONDUIT_MIDDLEWARE.md` §3 said an Author names a person "by the account name the identity provider knows them by". The Conduit has always compared a grant with the token's `sub` (`principal.id`, `principal_auth`), which is the account's identifier, and every stored grant — the seeds' included — is one. A grant made to a username was therefore not a typo but the same thing: it granted nothing to anyone. Nothing in the code changes; the documents now say what it does. The panel asks for an "Account id" and says where to find one: the Admin area shows each person's and each dashboard identity's (ADR-111 Amendment 2).
